subsections.title: Overview
subsections.summary: What it is and why it matters.

blocks.html: Personal data is any information that can be tied back to you: your name, address, phone number, location history, what you buy and what you search for. It is collected by the apps and sites you use, then bought and sold by data brokers who build profiles to sell to advertisers, landlords, employers — or anyone who pays. You can't stop all of it, but you can shrink how much is collected and remove a lot of what's already out there.

subsections.title: Terminology
subsections.summary: The words you will run into.

items.title: Data broker
items.html: A company that collects and sells profiles of people, usually without ever dealing with them directly.

items.title: People-search site
items.html: A broker that sells lookups of a person’s address, phone and relatives to the public.

items.title: Opt-out
items.html: A request asking a company to stop selling your data or to delete it.

items.title: Metadata
items.html: Data about data — like when and where a photo was taken — which can reveal more than the content.

items.title: GDPR / CCPA
items.html: EU and California privacy laws that give you the right to see and delete data held about you.

items.title: Advertising ID
items.html: A number your phone gives apps so advertisers can track you across them. You can delete it.

items.label: JustDeleteMe
items.desc: direct links to delete your accounts.

items.label: Have I Been Pwned
items.desc: check if your email appears in a known breach.
